title: A Garden for the Wolf
premise: In the city of Corvale, where magic was outlawed after the Dragon War, Ada Villalobos survives by hiding her gift for speaking with beasts behind a charm-seller's stall. When the crown's new hunt drags her neighbor—a child whose soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain—into the executioner's cart, Ada flees with a ragged found family of the hunted: a disgraced huntswoman, a fire-scarred fox, and an old jailer who knows the mountain's ways. To save the child, Ada must bargain with the dying last dragon, whose guttering fire keeps the stolen souls alive, and expose the chancellor who has been harvesting the gifted to fuel his own stolen magic. In the end, Ada gives up her own hidden memories of her lost mother to buy the souls back, and the freed dragon-fire burns the court's ledgers to ash—magic is still illegal, but the city learns to look away as Ada's garden of strays takes root in its cracks.
about_author: Ines Hartwell is the pen name of a former botanical illustrator who spent a decade drawing endangered plants before turning to fiction about endangered people. She writes from a drafty greenhouse studio, where her rescue animals are rumored to talk back.

chapters.title: Charms and Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. In Corvale's night market, Ada sells luck-charms and quietly soothes a cart-horse's fear, revealing her forbidden gift to the reader alone. A crown herald posts the Proclamation of the Hunt. The emotional beat is quiet dread: a fragile life built on hiding, about to crack.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Stopped Singing
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Her neighbor's son, Tam, goes gray-eyed and mute—his soul sold to the court beneath the mountain by a desperate father. Ada speaks with Tam's sparrow and learns the truth. The beat is grief curdling into resolve: she cannot stay invisible while children are hollowed out.

chapters.title: The Huntswoman's Debt
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren, a royal huntswoman ordered to sniff out the gifted, recognizes Ada's gift but owes Ada a life-debt from a fire years ago. She warns Ada instead of arresting her, and defects with a stolen writ. The beat is reluctant trust between two women on opposite sides of the law.

chapters.title: What the Jailer Buried
chapters.summary: Osk's POV. The old jailer who once guarded the mountain court smuggles the fugitives into the undercity, confessing he sold names to the chancellor to save his own daughter. The beat is guilt made flesh: complicity, apology, and the question of whether service can be atonement.

chapters.title: The Fox with the Burned Ear
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A fire-scarred fox leads the fugitives through the ash-roads, and Ada realizes the fox is a gifted girl transformed and lost. Bonding with her costs Ada her cover—a hunt patrol sees her speak. The beat is found family crystallizing just as the noose tightens.

chapters.title: Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The party descends into the court's vaults and finds the soul-ledgers: rows of names, Tam's among them, each kept alive by the last dragon's guttering flame. The beat is horror and awe—the machinery of injustice, and the dragon as both jailer and prisoner.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The dying dragon, Ember-that-Was, offers a trade: one soul freed for one memory surrendered. Ada learns the chancellor sold his own gift-harvest to the court and that her mother's soul is among the kept. The beat is temptation—Ada could buy her mother back instead of Tam.

chapters.title: Ledgers in Flame
chapters.summary: Osk and Maren's POV, alternating. While Ada bargains, Osk opens the vault doors and Maren holds the hunt patrol at bay, wounded. The fox-girl burns the ledger racks. The beat is sacrifice in motion: each member of the found family pays a piece of themselves for a stranger's child.

chapters.title: The Chancellor's Harvest
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, climax. Ada gives up her memories of her mother to free Tam's soul, then uses the dragon's last flame to expose the chancellor's stolen magic before the assembled court. The dragon-fire consumes the ledgers and the chancellor's power with them. The beat is the cost of justice: victory purchased with a piece of herself she can never reclaim.

chapters.title: A Garden for the Wolf
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, resolution. The dragon dies free; Tam wakes singing; the fox-girl regains her name, Sefi. Ada cannot remember her mother's face but plants a garden where her charms-stall stood, and the city's strays—human and beast—begin to gather there. The beat is bittersweet peace: memory lost, family found, justice living outside the law.
